newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek financial mkts shrug off low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Greek financial mkts shrug off low inflation.

text.p: Greek money, bond and forex markets showed indifference to a lower revised CPI inflation figure of 6.8 percent year-on-year in January fluctuating in narrow ranges holding morning levels in late dealings, said.
"The markets hardly reacted to news of a much lower inflation rate in January," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "All of them, cash, bonds and forex are idling."
The dealer said the decision of the central bank to keep its overnight bid unchanged at 12.40 percent took the wind out of the market's sails.

Many players fund bonds in the interbank market and the cost of carry is negative for those of them who do it through interbank depos. The short-end of the interbank yield curve depends on the Bank of Greece's overnight bid.
But bond funding through swaps can have a positive carry without counting unrealised capital gains from the nearly two-month bond old rally.
Consumer price inflation fell to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January from 7.3 percent in December. It stood at 7.5 percent in December based on the previous CPI index using 1988 for base year.
January inflation would have been at 7.1 percent year-on-year in January using the old CPI index.
The mark was quoted at 156.88/98 drachmas from Thursday's 156.880 fix, the dollar at 261.76/86 drachmas from 260.860 and the Ecu at 304.90/00 from 304.950 drachmas.
